note.text:
Chemistry safety rules:
• Wear safety goggles (and a lab coat) when heating or using acids and alkalis.
• Never taste anything. To smell a gas, waft it gently towards your nose with your hand.
• When diluting, add acid slowly to water, never water to acid.
• Point a test tube you are heating away from yourself and others.
• Label every container; never put chemicals in drink bottles.
• Do not return unused chemicals to the stock bottle; ask how to get rid of them.
• Wash spills on skin with plenty of water and tell the teacher at once.
• Wash your hands when you finish.

worked_example.problem: Ewane spills a little dilute acid on his hand. What should he do?
steps: Wash the hand at once under plenty of running water.
Do not rub the skin or put anything else on it unless the teacher says so.
worked_example.answer: Wash with plenty of water at once and tell the teacher.

cards.idea: Never taste chemicals, and never smell a gas directly: waft it towards your nose with your hand.
example: Waft: move your hand over the test tube to bring a little of the smell towards you.

cards.idea: When diluting, add acid to water, slowly. Point a heated test tube away from everyone.
example: Adding water to concentrated acid can make it boil and spit.

check.prompt: How should you dilute an acid?

right.text: Add the acid slowly to the water.

wrong.text: Add water quickly to the acid.
wrong.explain: Water added to concentrated acid can make it boil and spit.

wrong.text: Mix them in a drink bottle.
wrong.explain: Never use drink bottles for chemicals.
Heating the acid makes it more dangerous.

cards.idea: Spills on skin: wash with plenty of water at once and tell the teacher.
example: A splash in the eye: rinse with clean water for a long time and get help.

questions.prompt: Is each action safe or not safe in the chemistry laboratory?

pool.left: Wear safety goggles when heating or using acids.
Waft a smell towards your nose with your hand.
Add acid to water, slowly, not water to acid.
Point a heated test tube away from people.
Wash your hands after the practical.
Taste a chemical to identify it.

pick.a: Wash it with plenty of running water and tell the teacher.
pick.why: If acid splashes on your hand: Wash it with plenty of running water and tell the teacher.

pick.t: a chemical splashes into your eye
pick.a: Rinse the eye with clean water for a long time and get help at once.
pick.why: If a chemical splashes into your eye: Rinse the eye with clean water for a long time and get help at once.

pick.t: you smell gas from the Bunsen burner tap
pick.a: Turn off the gas, open windows and tell the teacher.
pick.why: If you smell gas from the Bunsen burner tap: Turn off the gas, open windows and tell the teacher.

pick.t: your classmate's test tube starts to spit while heating
pick.a: Move away and tell your classmate to point it away and stop heating.
pick.why: If your classmate's test tube starts to spit while heating: Move away and tell your classmate to point it away and stop heating.

misconceptions.explain: That is the right action for a different accident.

questions.prompt: Why must we never pour unused chemicals back into the stock bottle?

right.text: It could spoil (contaminate) the whole bottle for everyone.

wrong.explain: The danger is contaminating the whole stock bottle.

wrong.text: Because the bottle is too small.
wrong.explain: The real reason: the chemical may be dirty or mixed and spoil the stock.

wrong.text: Because the teacher wants to count them.
wrong.explain: The reason is safety and purity: it could contaminate the stock.

questions.prompt: One rule is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Wash your hands after a practical.
Waft a gas towards your nose to smell it.

wrong.explain: Always add acid to water, slowly.

wrong.text: You may keep a chemical in an empty drink bottle if you label it.
wrong.explain: Never use drink bottles: someone may drink from it.
